normalization_rule: Notebook results are C2 bounded model evidence; formal registries define proof obligations; failed executable-evidence audits remain failures and are not repaired by consistency with notebook outputs.

findings.title: Projection preserves coarse signature while permitting residue
findings.statement: Across Notebook 18's bounded projection model, a primitive signature can be retained while the projection emits residue and multiple organizations can share a resolution; this supports a candidate separation between invariant preservation and full information preservation.
findings.formal_statement: I_D(x)=I_D(y) does not imply x=y or R_D(x)=R_D(y) for a projection Pi_D unless injectivity and residue-completeness are separately established.

method: Notebook 18 resolution degeneracy and path comparison scaffold
counterexample_search.result: bounded degeneracy and path dependence reported

falsification_conditions: A governed model shows projection image plus declared domain determines all admissible residue without history or additional context.

findings.title: Distinction conservation is weaker than residue determinacy
findings.statement: Notebook 20 did not falsify distinction conservation in its tested model class, but strong residue determination was falsified by 478 matched-exclusion counterexamples; therefore conservation of a distinction measure should not be treated as sufficient to determine residue.
findings.formal_statement: Conservation_D(x_t)=Conservation_D(x_0) does not entail R(x_t)=f(Conservation_D(x_t)) for a single-valued f over the tested class.
falsification_conditions: Independent replication shows the 478 cases arise from a bookkeeping defect or that residue is uniquely determined after a correctly specified partition/history variable is included.

findings.title: History-augmented projection law
findings.statement: A more defensible continuation model may require residue to be parameterized by projection context and exclusion history rather than by the projected image alone.
findings.formal_statement: R_{D,t}=F(Pi_D(x_t), H_{exclusion,t}, C_t), where H_exclusion and C_t are explicit typed inputs and F is not assumed injective or universal.
falsification_conditions: Matched cases with identical projected image, context, and exclusion history but different residue remain after independent replication.
findings.recommended_next_action: Design a bounded Notebook 21 or formal fixture that varies projection image, context, and exclusion history independently, with immutable pre-execution specification and registered archive.

findings.title: Executable calculus evidence remains incomplete
findings.statement: The executable-evidence rerun is marked FAIL with 29 not-implemented validators, two inconclusive results, and two critical worktree-evidence failures; notebook consistency does not discharge this implementation debt.
findings.recommended_next_action: Treat executable-evidence completeness as a separate repair campaign and do not use C2 notebook outputs to claim calculus implementation validation.

open_branches: Repair executable-evidence validators and rerun failed gates.
deferred_branches: External physical interpretation of projection or residue.

termination_reason: Bounded corpus pass produced four non-duplicate discoveries and identified a focused frontier linking projection residue, exclusion history, D semantics, and executable-evidence debt.
what_this_does_not_authorize: It does not promote the conservation candidate to a theorem.
It does not establish universal projection or residue semantics.
It does not treat C2 notebook outputs as formal proof or implementation validation.
It does not close any debt or proof obligation.
